title: A conversation, in motion
summary: Voice agents turn sound into understanding—and understanding into a response.
points: Listen to a continuous stream of speech
Reason with the conversation and available tools
Respond naturally, and make room for interruptions
notes: Introduce the loop: listening, understanding, deciding and speaking. A voice agent is more than a chatbot with a speaker. Its parts need to coordinate in real time so the listener can interrupt and change direction. Keep this introduction to about twenty seconds.

title: From sound to meaning
summary: The first challenge is knowing what was said—and when the speaker is finished.
points: Microphone audio arrives in small chunks
Speech recognition interprets words and intent
Voice activity detection helps identify turns
notes: Explain that a microphone captures a waveform and streaming recognition interprets speech while audio continues arriving. Noise, accents and partial phrases can make interpretation uncertain. Voice activity detection distinguishes speech from pauses. In a native audio model some stages are integrated, rather than separate transcription services.

title: Context makes it a conversation
summary: A useful answer connects the new question to what the agent already knows.
points: Keep the conversation and full slide deck in context
Choose a relevant slide by meaning
Use a validated tool to change what is displayed
notes: Explain that context includes the deck, current slide and preceding questions. If someone asks how the agent knows when to stop, the system should infer the interruptions topic rather than require a slide number. The model requests a navigation tool, the application validates the request, changes the slide and acknowledges the result. Tool permissions are narrow.

title: Give the answer a voice
summary: Audio is streamed into a small playback queue, rather than waiting for a complete recording.
points: Generate speech with natural pacing and intonation
Schedule small audio chunks without gaps
Advance the slide only when playback finishes
notes: Describe streaming speech output, which reduces time to first sound. The application queues short PCM audio chunks and schedules them in order. Generation can finish before the audio has actually played, so the presenter waits for the browser playback queue to drain before advancing slides. No audio recording is saved by this prototype.

title: Good agents know when to stop
summary: An interruption should stop the old answer—not add another voice on top of it.
points: Detect the listener speaking while narration plays
Stop active audio and discard queued chunks
Answer the question, then resume the presentation
notes: Explain barge-in: the microphone stays active while the agent speaks. When the provider detects an interruption, the app stops current playback and clears queued audio. It tracks turns so old chunks cannot resume. A question can navigate to a different slide while preserving the presentation position. Headphones reduce echo and improve the demonstration.

title: One loop. Three boundaries.
summary: The browser handles the experience; a small backend keeps the provider credential private.
points: Browser: microphone, slide display and audio playback
Node backend: session state and validated navigation
Gemini Live: audio understanding, reasoning and speech
notes: Summarize the complete path: the browser streams microphone audio through the local Node backend to Gemini Live. Audio and tool requests return through the backend, which validates navigation and keeps the display synchronized. The permanent API key stays on the backend. End the presentation by inviting questions. Do not advance beyond this final slide.
